name: Declarative codebase: every widget and component written in the one syntax
description:
Approved by Antonio 2026-11-18 after a review showed much of the UI code built imperatively.

THE SYNTAX (what was established — the rule every item of this feature is brought to):
```rust
Component::new()
    .prop_a(..)                                    // its own typed properties, as builders
    .child(
        Grid::new()
            .template_row("auto 1fr")              // the arrangement is a track template
            .child([header, body]),                // children in order, composed to any depth
    )
    .on_click(|ev| ev.dispatch(Intent::new("an_action")))   // behaviour lives on the widget
```
Declarative and nested in one expression, Flutter/SwiftUI-shaped, DOM-shaped events. NEVER: find a child by position (children[0]), write a style/bound/position by hand, rebuild a widget to change one property, put a number in the code. If something cannot be written in this shape, the library is missing a builder — propose it (RULE ZERO), never work around it.
- Children list bound to data: the declarative form (ForEach / map-like, e.g. `.child(items.map(..))` reconciled by key) is NOT in the library yet. Keyed (docs/widgets.md:5743), on_props / set_props / reconcile_keyed (:5767) exist but are low-level and imperative (Keyed is host-only) — they are not the authoring form; a declarative API on top must be proposed and approved first.
- Props that change over time need a signal-bound form; many widgets lack it (e.g. Input placeholder/value).
- Behaviour: one click path for every activatable widget, every event reachable by plugins — owned by P087(F011)/T565 (approved plan in that task).
- heca-pro: the API it builds on (F012 surface) stays compatible — new form beside the old, removal agreed; heca-pro follows the same syntax.

WHERE IT IS WRITTEN (references):
- CLAUDE.md — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" block at the top (loaded in every session).
- AGENTS.md § 0 — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" and "⭐ heca-pro builds on heca — keep its API compatible, and it follows the same syntax".
- docs/widgets.md — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" block before "Mental model".
- Existing examples of the shape: docs/layout.md:35, :109, :143 ("The one rule"); docs/widgets.md:2342, :2360, :5683, :7029-7030 (.child([a, b])).
- heca-pro/AGENTS.md — "⭐ THE SYNTAX" section (written 2026-11-18, committed by Antonio).
- Project decisions: 05a2ed0c (the syntax), 15ec67fc (heca-pro compatibility + same syntax).
- PR #322 (merged 2026-11-18) put the blocks into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/widgets.md.

CURRENT STATE (grep scan on main 2026-11-18, indicative only — the full review is step 1):
- Library widgets with children found by position: dialog 13, input 9, tree_layout 6, overlay 5, tile 4, command_palette 3, flex 3, resizable 3, message_list 2, tag 2, visibility 2.
- Library widgets positioning by hand (bounds writes / shift_subtree): command_palette 4, select 4, overlay 2, context_menu 2, scroll_region 2 (scroll_region/motion.rs:66), scroll_bar 2, toast 2, marker_group 2, badge_button 1, flex 1.
- Many numeric literals: key_hint 18, overlay 16, button 13, item 11, command_palette 11; Pane padding 8.0 (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/pane/mod.rs:60).
- App: terminal component lays itself out by writing style fields (heca/src/chrome/panes/terminal/component/mod.rs:103-108; search/mod.rs:218-220, focus by index :267); chrome/window; sidebar spots (providers/workspaces/column_group.rs:137 writes bounds; row_lines.rs:228, pane_row.rs:552 children by index); heca/src/components 6 index reads; the command palette (P087(F011)/T469, paused, uncommitted rewrite in heca-feat-469 still imperative).
- Described plugins have only press/change/toggle events (docs/widgets.md:7259).

PLAN (agreed):
1. Read-only review of every library widget (~60) and every app component against THE SYNTAX: per item, defects with file:line and a verdict (ok / fix / rewrite). Then one task per item, created with Antonio's consent.
2. Library first: declarative child list (proposal first), signal-bound props where needed, T565. Most-used widgets first (dialog, input, overlay, select, scroll_region, flex, tree_layout, tile, button, command_palette), then app (terminal, window, sidebar, palette).
3. Each item: done by the orchestrator without sub-agents, reviewed line by line against THE SYNTAX before Antonio's eye-check, one PR each.
ESTIMATE (2026-11-18, before the review): ~40–80 hours of work + 25–35 PRs to eye-check (~6–12 full days), revised after step 1.

acceptedDecisions.title: A property that changes is bound in the builder, never set on a built widget
acceptedDecisions.decision: Every builder property accepts either a fixed value or a value that changes (a Signal), under the same name and in the same place in the chain — THE SYNTAX unchanged. Whoever wants the property to change changes the STATE, never the widget: `let name = signal(..); Label::new(name); name.set(..)`. Layout and paint follow by themselves. This applies to every widget property AND to Base's style (layout and visual). It is the same model `.child(rooms.map(RoomRow::new))` (T569) already uses for children. Agreed with Antonio 2026-11-19 ("Sì").
acceptedDecisions.rationale:
Reaching into a built widget to set something (`label.text_signal().set(..)`, `row.state().set(true)`) is the imperative form; it is not THE SYNTAX, and it forced side tables of handles keyed by id. Flutter/SwiftUI bind a property to state where the property is written.

SHAPE DECIDED (Antonio, 2026-11-19, "Forma 1"): in native code the property itself accepts the signal — `Label::new(name)`, `.active(active)`, `.template_column(cols)` — the same builder takes a fixed value or a Signal. Not a separate `.bind("prop", signal)` next to the property (form 2, rejected for native code: the property written twice, its name a string that a typo breaks only at run time). Described plugins (ViewNode, WASM/RPC) cannot hold a signal and keep T360's `.text("Running").bind("text", "daemon_status")`; `realize` turns that binding into form 1 by passing the value store's signal to the builder (`Label::new(signal)`). So a described plugin is written the same whichever native form; a native plugin (heca-pro, heca::extension) writes form 1.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Library: one "value or signal" mechanism written once (no per-widget copy), every builder takes it; the layout engine records the signals a widget reads while measured (heca-grid-ui/src/layout/build.rs: apply_bound / remeasure / taffy_style / measure_text) and asks for layout when one changes; paint likewise. Then the window uses heca_grid_ui::needs_layout (the contract already documented in docs/widgets.md § "Asking the host to lay the tree out again") instead of laying out every frame — see project decision 06ac6e43 for why that was not done in T572.

acceptedDecisions.title: Base's fields stay public, like a DOM element's
acceptedDecisions.decision: `Base`'s fields (style, children, the visible/disabled/focused signals) stay public — heca and heca-pro use them the way a DOM element's properties are used. No field is made private to enforce layout updates. Antonio 2026-11-19: "heca-pro dovrebbe poter usare campi come si fa in un DOM element. non vedo perche' debbano essere privati."
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Rejected proposals of the same day: making style/children private behind methods, and a wrapper type that notices writes. The library already has the contract for structural changes (docs/widgets.md § needs_layout: mark_needs_layout, set_hidden guarded by a test); changing properties goes through bound signals (the decision above), so no field needs hiding.

acceptedDecisions.title: How a widget property changes today — three ways, two of them to remove (review of 2026-11-19)
acceptedDecisions.decision: Found in the code on 2026-11-19, to be brought to the bound form: (1) the widget keeps the signal and the caller takes the handle out after building it, storing it in side tables keyed by id — `ChromeSignals` (heca/src/chrome/window/signals.rs:26: pane_active, pane_previous, col_active, ws_active, ws_previous, row nav…) then `.set(..)` — imperative and a registry, against RULE ZERO: TO REMOVE; (2) the window tree is rebuilt when a state fingerprint changes (`chrome_signature`, heca/src/chrome/window/retained) — changing a property by rebuilding, against THE SYNTAX; also the source of ~19 ms layout spikes: TO REMOVE; (3) a builder takes the signal directly (`with_text_signal`, `with_max_lines_signal`, `with_mode_signal` — 13 uses) plus `.child(signal.map(..))`: the right form, to make the only one.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Inventory of the 56 widgets in heca-grid-ui (.planner/docs/f013-widget-properties-2026-11-19.md): 77 properties live (signals); ~110 widget properties fixed at construction; all of Base.style is plain fields nothing follows; ~120 fields are internal state (not properties). 22 widgets have no live property of their own, among them the ones that give the shape: Flex, Grid, Surface, Card, Pane, Overlay, Dialog, Button. Flex/Surface/Card/Tile/Panel/KeyHint/Tooltip/TreeLayout have no own properties — what they are is Base.style. Heaviest fixed ones: Grid template (columns, rows, areas), Button label/variant/glyph/active, Overlay position/panel_size/blocking, Pane frame/border, Label align/color/truncate, Row marker/colours, ScrollRegion axes/scrollbars/follow_bottom.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: This inventory is the "properties" part of F013 step 1 (the read-only review); the rest of step 1 (children by position, hand positioning, numeric literals, per-item verdict) is still to do. Proposed order (not yet confirmed by Antonio): Base.style first (unlocks every container at once), then Grid and Button, then the rest. Estimate for the properties part, agent time: value-or-signal mechanism + engine tracking 2–3 h; Base.style bindable ~2–3 h; ~110 widget properties with a test each 6–10 h; heca moved to the bound form (ChromeSignals tables and chrome_signature rebuilds gone, window uses needs_layout) 6–10 h; docs 1–2 h — ~17–28 h over several sessions, plus Antonio's eye-checks after Base, after the widgets, at the end. The F013 description's line "the declarative child list is NOT in the library yet" is outdated: T569 added `.child(items.map(..))`.

acceptedDecisions.title: AGENTS.md's SETTLED row shows the imperative form as the example — to correct
acceptedDecisions.decision: AGENTS.md (⭐ SETTLED table, the row "Then move ViewNode down into the library?", line ~1428) and docs/widget-architecture.md § 2 cite `row.state().set(true)` and `label.text_signal().set(…)` as how the native chrome updates in place. Their purpose there is to defend signals against routing everything through ViewNode, not to show how to write a widget — but they present the imperative form as the model, and nowhere in AGENTS.md is the bound form shown, so it got copied. To correct to the bound form (`Label::new(name)` with name a Signal; `.child(rooms.map(..))`; change the state, not the widget) — only after Antonio has gone through it ("Non modificare. Devi capire." 2026-11-19: a first edit was reverted).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Agents copy the examples they see; the only example of an update after construction in the file every agent reads is the imperative one.

acceptedDecisions.title: T360 is the plugin half of the same work and depends on bindable native properties
acceptedDecisions.decision: P085(F003)/T360 (a per-mount value store a plugin writes, and `ViewNode` bindings `.text("Running").bind("text", "daemon_status")`) binds a described property by binding "the widget's signal". It can bind only properties that have a signal — 77 today. So F013's bound properties come first; T360 then uses them. No new task and no widening of T360 for the native work: it belongs to F013 (Antonio, 2026-11-19).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Keeps one owner per capability: F013 owns native bindable properties and the bound form; T360 owns the described/plugin side and the value store.
